title: The Autonomy Audit: A New Work Scenario
instructions: 阅读下面的短文，完成10道题目。短文和题目均为英语，解释为中文。所有情景与数据均为模拟教学材料，并非真实事件或官方考试。请先通读全文，再作答。
passage:
A. When the management of a mid-sized logistics company announced a new scheduling system, most employees expected little change. The system, they were told, would simply help the company respond faster to customer orders. However, within three months, some workers noticed that their daily routines had shifted in unexpected ways. Drivers reported that the software suggested routes they had not chosen themselves. Warehouse staff said that their break times were now set by an algorithm rather than by their team leader. These small adjustments, according to several employees, gradually reduced their sense of control over their own work.

B. Dr. Lena Ortiz, a workplace researcher, argues that such changes are rarely neutral. She claims that when a system decides how tasks are distributed, it also decides who has the authority to make decisions. In her view, employees often accept these tools because they promise efficiency, but they may not realize how much discretion they are giving up. She points out that some managers welcome the data these systems provide, while others worry that the tools undermine their own judgment. Ortiz suggests that companies should ask a simple question before adopting any new technology: who gains and who loses control?

C. Not all workers experience automation in the same way. A survey of 400 employees in the logistics sector found that most respondents valued the predictability of automated schedules. They said they could plan their family time more easily. However, a significant minority—about one in five—reported feeling monitored and stressed. These workers said they had less freedom to adjust their pace when they were tired or unwell. The survey also revealed that all participants wanted clearer information about how the system made its decisions. None of them had been consulted before the system was introduced.

D. Some companies have responded by creating “autonomy audits.” In these audits, managers and employees review together how much choice workers actually have in their daily tasks. The goal is not to reject technology but to balance efficiency with professional autonomy. According to one warehouse supervisor, the audit helped his team identify three areas where the software could be adjusted to allow more flexible breaks. He said, “We didn’t need to throw out the system. We just needed to talk about what mattered.”

E. Critics, however, remain skeptical. They argue that autonomy audits can become a public-relations exercise if senior leaders do not genuinely share power. One critic noted that most audits focus on small adjustments while ignoring larger questions about who designs the algorithms in the first place. Unless workers have a real voice in the design process, she warned, such audits may simply make employees feel better without changing the underlying balance of control. The debate, it seems, is far from over.

grammar.title: 转述动词与限定词的范围
grammar.explanation: 在英语中，转述别人的话时常用转述动词，如 say, claim, argue, suggest, point out, warn 等。不同的转述动词可以表达不同的态度：claim 常暗示说话者不一定同意；argue 表示有论据地主张；suggest 表示提出建议或可能性。另外，限定词 some, most, all 表示范围大小：some 指“一些”（不是全部），most 指“大多数”（超过一半但非全部），all 指“全部”。使用时要根据事实选择准确的限定词，避免夸大或缩小范围。
grammar.example: She claims that when a system decides how tasks are distributed, it also decides who has the authority to make decisions.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The researcher ______ that the new policy will reduce creativity, but she did not provide evidence.
questions.explanation: claim 表示“声称”，常暗示缺乏证据，符合句意。
questions.evidence: She claims that when a system decides how tasks are distributed, it also decides who has the authority to make decisions.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The manager ______ that the team should take more breaks during busy periods.
questions.explanation: suggest 表示“建议”，后接 that 从句，符合语境。
questions.evidence: Ortiz suggests that companies should ask a simple question before adopting any new technology: who gains and who loses control?

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The critic ______ that most audits focus on small adjustments while ignoring larger questions.
questions.explanation: point out 表示“指出”，用于转述批评者的观点。
questions.evidence: One critic noted that most audits focus on small adjustments while ignoring larger questions about who designs the algorithms in the first place.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The supervisor ______ that the audit helped his team identify three areas for improvement.
questions.explanation: said 是最中性的转述动词，符合直接引述的转述。
questions.evidence: He said, “We didn’t need to throw out the system. We just needed to talk about what mattered.”

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The report ______ that all participants wanted clearer information.
questions.explanation: reveal 表示“揭示、透露”，用于转述调查结果。
questions.evidence: The survey also revealed that all participants wanted clearer information about how the system made its decisions.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The critic ______ that autonomy audits may simply make employees feel better without changing the balance of control.
questions.explanation: warn 表示“警告”，符合批评者提出潜在风险的语境。
questions.evidence: she warned, such audits may simply make employees feel better without changing the underlying balance of control.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The article ______ that some managers welcome the data, while others worry about losing judgment.
questions.explanation: note 表示“指出、提到”，用于客观转述文章内容。
questions.evidence: She points out that some managers welcome the data these systems provide, while others worry that the tools undermine their own judgment.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: The employees ______ that the software suggested routes they had not chosen themselves.
questions.explanation: report 表示“报告、反映”，用于转述员工的反馈。
questions.evidence: Drivers reported that the software suggested routes they had not chosen themselves.
